title: Fit two brake pads facing the rotor, then swing the caliper down over them
instruction: Fit both new brake pads in the bracket with their linings facing the rotor, then swing the red caliper down over them.
context: Automotive service technicians (O*NET 49-3023.00) and bus and truck mechanics (49-3031.00) change disc brake pads by dropping each pad's steel ears into the bracket's slots with the lining toward the rotor, then pivoting the caliper down over both. A pad fitted backwards puts steel against the rotor. Board tasks with the same shape: 'Set a sand core in its prints, then close the cope between the guide posts' (insert, then close) and 'Seat the filter cartridge with its flow arrow pointing downstream' (one part, one direction). This one adds two mirror-image parts, each turned the opposite way to face a shared rotor, and a closure that cannot shut until both are fully down.
setup: Positions are object centres in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward (away from the arms), y to the robot's left (negative toward the right arm). Table: wood top, about 110 x 130 cm, arm bases 61 cm apart (y +30.5 and -30.5) on its near edge. Brake, all fixed to the table: a dark grey steel carrier base, 10 x 14 x 3 cm, centred at x 27, y -4. On it, a light grey steel rotor plate standing on edge, 2 x 16 x 8 cm tall (x 26 to 28, y -12 to 4). Two dark grey steel abutment blocks, each 10 x 3 x 4.5 cm on the base (x 22 to 32): one at y -11 to -8, one at y 0 to 3. Each has two vertical ear slots cut in its inner face, 1.2 cm wide and 1 cm deep, centred at x 23.9 and x 30.1, with floors 3.5 cm above the table. Two near-black steel pad stops, 1.3 x 8 x 4 cm on the base (top 7 cm above the table), at x 22 to 23.3 and x 30.7 to 32, y -8 to 0. A dark grey steel hinge post, 8 x 1.5 x 8.5 cm, at x 27, y 3 to 4.5. Caliper: a dark red painted steel bridge, 9 x 14 x 2 cm, 150 g with its post, hinged about a horizontal axis along x at y 3.5, 12 cm above the table; closed it lies at y -10.5 to 3.5, 12 to 14 cm up, 0.5 cm above the seated pads. A bright red 2 x 2 x 3 cm post stands on the bridge's top face at x 27, 7 cm from the hinge. It starts swung up 100 degrees from closed (10 degrees past upright, leaning toward +y) against its stop, hinge damped. Pads (two, identical): each 60 g, a silver steel backing plate 0.6 x 9 x 5 cm, a dark brown friction lining 1.4 x 7 x 4 cm on one face, and an orange plastic grip tab 1.8 x 4 x 3 cm on top. Each stands upright in a blue plastic holder (a 10 x 4.2 x 0.4 cm tray with two 10 x 0.8 x 3 cm cheek walls, 2.6 cm apart inside), pad centre at x 20.5, y -23 and at x 20.5, y -14.5, with its lining toward +y; each pad is turned a quarter turn to face the rotor, one each way. Seated: ears on the slot floors, tab top 11.5 cm above the table.
scoring: At the end of the run (grippers opened), measured with a ruler and a top photo. 0 if any part of a pad is over the rotor (x 26 to 28, y -12 to 4). Otherwise a pad is seated when its ears are in both slots of one pair (plate bottom within 3 mm of the slot floor, plate middle within 4 mm of the slot middle and 3 mm of y -4, tilt at most 10 degrees) with its lining turned to the rotor (within 6 degrees); each pair takes one pad. 0.25 for one pad seated; 0.5 for both seated; 1.0 for both seated and the caliper closed (post within 4 mm of resting on its stop), everything still. A pad turned lining-outward, perched on the stops or abutments, or held in the air is not seated. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0.
reset_notes: Stand both pads upright in their holders, linings toward +y, and swing the caliper back up against its stop. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid parts, default friction; the caliper hinge is damped, with no latch, spring or piston. The simulator scores the last step without opening the grippers, so a held pad never scores better than a released one: a pad whose bottom is over 1 cm above every support counts as not seated, and any pad over the rotor, at any height, scores 0. The arms' path is not scored.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (reached over the pad holders with the right arm, caliper stayed up); demo: 1.0 (moved both pads from holders into the brake, then swung the caliper closed)
